notice.title: Keeping complaint records
notice.aiSummary: Firms must retain all complaint records and correspondence for at least 7 years from the final response and provide them to the Authority within 10 business days of a request. Compliance is required by 2027-01-15.
notice.aiReason: The notice applies to all firms that handle complaints from retail customers, and Brivanta Bank handles retail customer complaints across its consumer and small-business banking products.

text:
RETAIL CONDUCT AUTHORITY FICTIONAL REGULATOR - SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE
Guidance: Keeping complaint records
Notice number: RCN-2026-007
Issued by: Retail Conduct Authority
Published: 2026-09-22
Effective date: 2027-01-15
1. Who this applies to
All firms that handle complaints from retail customers.
2. Background
Supervisors reviewing complaint handling often find that the original correspondence has already been deleted. Complete records are needed to review how a complaint was handled.
3. Requirements
3.1 A firm must retain records of each complaint, including all correspondence with the customer, for at least 7 years from the final response.
3.2 A firm must provide complaint records to the Authority within 10 business days of a request.
4. Status
Firms must comply with the requirements in section 3 from 2027-01-15.

obligations.text: A firm must retain records of each complaint, including all correspondence with the customer, for at least 7 years from the final response.
obligations.controlDesc: Weekly report of complaints open for more than 30 calendar days without a final response, escalated to the head of Customer Care
obligations.reason: Policy POL-REC-01 requires customer communications including complaint correspondence to be deleted after 5 years, which is a shorter retention period than the 7 years required by the obligation, creating a direct conflict that prevents the obligation from being met.
obligations.conflictReason: Policy A retains complaint files for 7 years after the final response (matching the obligation), but Policy B deletes customer communications including complaint correspondence after only 5 years from creation, which would violate the 7-year retention requirement for complaints.

obligations.text: A firm must provide complaint records to the Authority within 10 business days of a request.
obligations.controlDesc: Daily report of complaints not acknowledged within 2 business days, reviewed by the complaints manager
obligations.reason: Policy POL-REC-02 states that regulatory requests are "answered within the deadline set by the supervisor, or within 10 business days if none is given," which matches the obligation's 10 business day requirement for providing complaint records to the Authority.
